mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% for two consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% for 2 months but S&P 500 5-day returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal weakening demand that reduces corporate revenue visibility, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS decline simultaneously but S&P 500 20-day returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 95.0) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) signals a supply shock that increases corporate costs and reduces profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY but S&P 500 60-day returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth rate (3-month moving average) indicates labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth rate increases but S&P 500 20-day returns negative in >60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 1.5% MoM) combined with rising residential construction (HOUST > 0.5% MoM) signals robust economic activity that supports earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 1.5% MoM and HOUST > 0.5% MoM but S&P 500 60-day returns negative in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate manufacturing sector weakness and labor market contraction that signal economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline and UNRATE rise simultaneously but S&P 500 20-day returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.
